    - Each element in the result sequence should be the sum of the corresponding elements in a and b

Step 1: Determine the method’s signature.

Step 2: Determine the preconditions.

Step 3: Determine the postconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - The result sequence should contain the element-wise sums of the input sequences
    
Dafny specification:
    ensures result != null
    ensures result.Length == a.Length

Step 4: Write the code, its formal specification, and the verification annotations that help the solver prove the postconditions.
In this case:

```dafny
method ElementWiseAdd(a: seq<int>, b: seq<int>) returns (result: seq<int>)
    requires a != null && b != null
    requires a.Length == b.Length
    ensures result != null
    ensures result.Length == a.Length
    ensures forall i :: 0 <= i < a.Length ==> result[i] == a[i] + b[i]
{
    result := [];
    var i := 0;
    while i < a.Length
        invariant 0 <= i <= a.Length
        invariant result == a[..i] + b[..i]
    {
        result := result + [a[i] + b[i]];
        i := i + 1;
    }
}
```
